list: Typically, Professional positions require judgment in analyzing and evaluating problems as well as in decision-making involving discretionary choices between alternative courses of action.

What we are looking for in a candidate for P or D position?

We are looking for highly skilled and motivated candidates with the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, whilst paying due regard to geographical and gender diversity. We seek talent that is committed to our mission and values. Our three core values are timeless and universal principles that apply to all of us in the UN family: i) We live and act with Integrity, ii) We show Professionalism and iii) We respect diversity.

Directors represent the highest level in this category and on the career staffing structure. As a Director, you are also expected to provide leadership in formulating and implementing the substantive work programme of an office, determine priorities, and allocate resources for the completion of outputs and their timely delivery.

sections.paragraph: The General Service category contributes to the execution of the programmes of the organization through work that is procedural, operational, technical, or para-professional in nature. The functions of General Service support are central to efficient service delivery within the Organization. The work ranges from routine or repetitive work to functions that are varied and complex in nature. Routine work is undertaken in line with detailed instructions while complex work requires identification and consideration of alternative courses of action based on extensive and in-depth practical knowledge of a specific subject area.

sections.heading: What education and work experience do you need for General Service positions?
sections.paragraph: Completion of higher secondary education with high school diploma or equivalent is our standard educational requirement for all General Service level positions and we apply the following standard recruitment requirements for these positions: Please refer to “Minimum Requirements” outlined in each individual vacancy announcement for further details and the specific qualifications required for each position.

sections.heading: What we are looking for in a candidate for General Service positions?
sections.paragraph: We are looking for highly motivated staff capable of achieving results in administrative, operational, procedural and technical capacities. We seek talent who can handle routine to complex tasks with dedication, and who are committed to our mission and values. Our three core values are timeless and universal principles that apply to all of us in the UN family: i) We live and act with Integrity. ii) We show Professionalism. We respect diversity. We also want someone who is an excellent team player and who can think outside the box and innovate.

sections.paragraph: Project (L) Appointments are non-career appointments that provide capacity and functions for specific programmes/projects for a specified period of time, i.e. they will not subsist beyond the lifetime of the programmes/projects that finance such appointments. Individuals holding a project appointment have the status of staff member of UNIDO. Project appointments may be utilized for professional or general support functions. Irrespective of the length of project appointment and the category, staff under project appointments carry no expectancy of conversion, extension, or renewal of the contract.

sections.heading: What education and work experience do you need for Project Appointments?
sections.paragraph: Education and work experience requirements for project appointments follow UNIDO recruitment standards as per the required category, i.e. International Professionals, National Professional Officers and General Service (links embedded).

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.paragraph: The benefits offered follow our standard benefits package, as per the category of project appointment, which is outlined on the respective job posting. Please see the UNIDO brochure for further information.

UNIDO employs many consultants and other support personnel under Individual Service Agreement (ISA) contracts to help UNIDO to meet its Organizational mandate, namely in the area of technical cooperation programmes and projects. ISA holders are considered non-staff members of UNIDO who have a legal status as individual contractors to the Organization. There are three main categories of ISA holders: International Consultants, National Consultants and Local Support Personnel.

sections.heading: Fields in which UNIDO hires ISA holders:

sections.heading: What is the JPO Programme?
sections.paragraph: The JPO Programme provides an opportunity to professionals to gain work experience, receive training, and be exposed to the work of UNIDO. Specific assignments may vary depending on specific donor interests and mutual agreement of both parties. JPOs are recruited under bilateral agreements between UNIDO and donor member states. They are appointed under fixed-term contracts to posts funded by the respective donor government and currently donor governments only sponsor nationals of their own countries.

sections.heading: Impact for Member States
sections.paragraph: The JPO Programme is a unique opportunity for donors, to sponsor professionals to acquire valuable work experience in the field of international cooperation and development. It is also an opportunity for these nationals to launch their career in one of the organizations of the UN system. JPOs bring the diversity that is essential to the workforces of international organizations. JPOs also support key priority areas of UNIDO’s work and in many cases, such areas are also aligned closely to donor’s development cooperation activities. Placements of JPOs may be proposed based on national development cooperation strategies. Likewise, efforts shall be made to place JPOs in priority areas of UNIDO, ensuring mutual benefits to both. Donors would announce the job profile for a process of competitive selection at the national level, resulting in a final shortlist of candidates recommended to UNIDO’s Director General for further selection.

sections.heading: Desired Profile of a JPO – General requirements

rows.Age: Depends on donor country, usually below 32 at the time of application
rows.Education: Advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in a relevant field
rows.Experience: A minimum of 3 years of professional work experience is required for appointment at the L-2 level
rows.Languages: Fluency in English is required. Working knowledge of another UN official language (French, Spanish, ArabicChinese, Russian) is an asset.

sections.heading: What is expected of a JPO?
sections.paragraph: When joining UNIDO, the JPO is expected to (a) contribute to UNIDO established practices and priority areas; (b) undertake assignments that include staff and career development elements for the JPO; and (c) receive proper supervision by the immediate supervisor.

sections.heading: What is the programme’s duration?
sections.paragraph: The usual duration of the JPO programme is 24 months. Upon the donor's request, this may be extended to 36 months or shortened to 12 months.

sections.heading: Countries currently Supporting the JPO Programme at UNIDO
sections.paragraph: For statistics on our JPO programme, please visit JPO Facts and Figures (link). UNIDO is grateful to its Member States such as China, Finland, Germany, Italy and Japan, to name a few, for currently supporting the JPO programme.

sections.heading: How can a JPO Donor Agreement be secured?
sections.paragraph: An exchange of communications can be triggered by any of the parties, whether it is a Representative to International Organizations based in Vienna or through UNIDO’s Strategic Donor Relations Division. The end result shall be a signed Agreement. For more information, please email us: recruitment@unido.org Please see the JPO Programme Brochure for further information.

sections.heading: Other Resources:
What is the Partner Experts Programme?
sections.paragraph: Partner Experts (PEs) are qualified experts who are provided to UNIDO under bilateral agreements between partner institutions and UNIDO at no direct cost to UNIDO. The programme aims to expand our partnership with member states, donors and partner institutions in contributing valuable human capital to the Organization. The programme offers challenging projects and assignments in different areas of UNIDO’s activities.

sections.heading: Impact for Sponsors
sections.paragraph: The PE Programme gives donor Member States or partner institutions a unique opportunity to sponsor their qualified experts to gain valuable international experience working in UNIDO. PEs would be in a position to promote specific projects in the global development sector which are mutually beneficial to both parties. It is also envisioned that PEs are highly qualified subject-matter experts who can share their expertise with a wider audience as part of their Corporate Social Responsibilities. UNIDO highly values its partnerships with member states, donors and partner institutions sponsoring PEs.

sections.heading: Key impact for Partner Experts
sections.paragraph: Opportunity to collaborate with peers in the field of international development cooperation and management and promote specific mutually beneficial projects in the global development sector; Working in a diverse and multi-cultural environment; Being exposed to the work of specialized organizations of the United Nations; Become part of UNIDO’s resource pool of talents; PEs are trusted to provide specialized professional input in the areas of UNIDO's business. sections.heading: What is the programme's duration?
sections.paragraph: The duration of a PE assignment is for a minimum of six months and a maximum of 24 months. PEs shall have a relationship to UNIDO as an independent contractor and are thus not staff members of UNIDO. Their relationship to UNIDO is established by an individual service agreement. The sponsoring entity provides the full range of the PE’s remuneration, entitlements including their social security and travel to and from their country to the duty station.

sections.paragraph: A sponsoring entity wishing to participate in the PE programme shall conclude a Memorandum of Agreement with UNIDO. For further information please email: Staff.Services@unido.org

title: Recruitment Practices at UNIDO: Rules, Processes and Reference Materials

sections.heading: Recruitment Practices at UNIDO: Rules, Processes and Reference Materials
sections.paragraph: This page provides further detail on the rules, policies and reference materials that inform recruitment at UNIDO. It is intended for Permanent Mission representatives seeking a clearer understanding of how recruitment is governed and how related frameworks on diversity, gender equality, ethics and organizational culture connect to talent acquisition.

rows.Column_1: 1. Regulatory basis for recruitment
Recruitment at UNIDO is governed first and foremost by the Organization’s official legal and administrative framework.
Core legal references
Staff Regulations and Rules UNIDO Code of Ethical Conduct
Key principle from the regulatory framework

A core principle of the UNIDO regulatory framework is that the paramount consideration in employment is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, while due regard is paid to the importance of recruiting staff on a wide and equitable geographical basis.
2. What this means in practice

In practical terms, UNIDO recruitment is designed to attract qualified candidates through publicly advertised vacancy announcements, assess applicants against post-specific requirements, and apply consistent processes that support fairness, integrity and equal treatment. It also supports inclusive outreach and workforce diversity, including gender balance and wide and equitable geographical representation, while maintaining merit as the foundation of selection.
3. Careers pages relevant to candidates and Member States

Permanent Missions may wish to use these pages when directing prospective applicants to the appropriate category and to the official vacancy notice, which remains the authoritative source for post-specific requirements.
Staff categories and programmes

UNIDO offers different contract modalities and programmes, which may vary depending on the type of opportunity and the applicable vacancy announcement. Permanent Mission representatives are encouraged to visit careers.unido.org for current information on available categories, programmes and application details.
4. Gender equality and inclusive recruitment

UNIDO’s approach to gender equality in recruitment is grounded in its policy and official public materials on gender equality and women’s empowerment, which set the broader institutional direction for inclusive talent outreach and representation.

In practice, recruitment supports the hiring of women by combining merit-based selection with measures that help broaden the pool of qualified female applicants and reinforce fair processes. This can include inclusive vacancy communication, targeted outreach to women professionals and relevant networks, and attention to diversity in assessment settings. Beyond recruitment, HRM also helps advance gender equality through learning and awareness initiatives, leadership and career development support such as women-dedicated events and mentoring programmes, policy guidance, and workplace standards that promote respectful conduct and equal opportunity. Permanent Mission representatives may also wish to consult the Women in Industrial Development page for broader information on some of the many talented women working at UNIDO.
To learn more about HRM’s work in this area, we recommend you read the UNIDO Roadmap on Workforce Related Gender Equality here.
5. Geographical representation

UNIDO recognizes wide and equitable geographical representation as an important dimension of workforce diversity. Permanent Missions can support this objective by helping qualified nationals access accurate information on vacancies and application requirements.
How this is being advanced in practice

UNIDO’s strategy on wide and equitable geographical representation emphasizes targeted outreach, stronger engagement with Member States, expanded talent pipelines and recruitment process enhancements.

In practice, this includes promoting UNIDO as an employer of choice via our Webinar Outreach Programme in multiple formats and official languages, conducting recruitment bootcamps that help applicants better understand and prepare for UNIDO selection processes, as well as other UN organizations, stronger online presence through careers content and targeted employer branding, and partnership-based dissemination of opportunities through Member States, universities and professional networks. It also includes pipeline measures such as youth-focused programmes and internships, together with the use of data and recruitment monitoring to identify gaps and support more informed outreach efforts. For information on the profiles attracted in some of our outreach programmes, please click here to view the UNIDO Webinar Infographics and click here to view the significant increase of applications at UNIDO between 2024 and 2025.

For more information, please visit careers.unido.org to find youth dedicated programmes such as the Junior Professional Officers, Paid Internships, Industrial Future Talent Initiative and more. Click here.
UNIDO’s Webinar Outreach Programme presentations can be found on our official playlist on YouTube and Weibo.
Recruitment Bootcamps

The Recruitment Bootcamp proposal is designed as a practical outreach and capacity-building initiative to help potential applicants better understand UNIDO’s recruitment processes and strengthen their ability to compete for opportunities. Member States, universities and professional organizations can support this initiative by sponsoring workshops and covering related delivery costs, such as travel and daily subsistence for participating recruiters, and by helping convene relevant audiences and local partners for implementation.
For more information on the agenda and costs, please click here for our proposal.
For more information on UNIDO’s Geographical Representation strategy, please read our official document here.
6. Ethics, accountability and respectful conduct
Recruitment also operates within UNIDO’s wider accountability and ethics framework, which reinforces standards of professionalism, respect, non-discrimination, and responsible conduct.
Relevant references

Transparency and Accountability UNIDO Code of Ethical Conduct Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Policy on the Prohibition, Prevention and Resolution of Harassment, including Sexual Harassment, Discrimination and Abuse of Authority
7. Values and Behaviours framework

UNIDO’s evolving organizational culture and talent management approach are also supported by a Values and Behaviours framework intended to provide a shared reference point for how people are expected to work, lead and collaborate across the Organization once publicly available. This is important across HRM functions because it helps align recruitment with the behaviours sought in candidates, supports learning and development by clarifying the capabilities and conduct the Organization aims to strengthen, and informs performance management by creating a more consistent basis for feedback, development conversations and expectations.
Relevant reference
Values and Behaviours Framework
8. Role of Permanent Missions

Permanent Missions can play a practical role in supporting UNIDO’s recruitment and outreach efforts by engaging with HRM on talent attraction initiatives, helping disseminate vacancy announcements through national, regional and sector-specific professional organizations and associations, and promoting awareness of UNIDO career opportunities among qualified audiences. They may also support outreach activities more directly by facilitating or financing recruitment bootcamps at universities and professional associations in their respective countries, promoting webinars and related engagement formats that help potential candidates better understand UNIDO’s recruitment processes and prepare more effectively to compete for opportunities.

Important note: This page is provided for general information only. In all cases, the applicable official vacancy announcement, the promulgated regulatory framework, and any relevant administrative issuances remain the authoritative reference. For more information, visit careers.unido.org or contact recruitment@unido.org.
